import numpy as np
from scipy import stats

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Filter out near-duplicates based on correlation
    keep_ids = set(feats.ids)
    corr_pairs = [
        (a, b) for a, b in [
            ("TPMH13", "EPWQ12B"), ("SCL4", "EPWQ12B"), ("BHKP6", "VWC7B"),
            ("SWH9", "JXR1P"), ("EPWQ12B", "JTJT5B"), ("YZN7L", "EPWQ12B"),
            ("JXR1P", "EPWQ12B"), ("SCL4", "TPMH13"), ("CMUA7", "EPWQ12B"),
            ("EPWQ12B", "CBZ3"), ("TPMH13", "TCN17"), ("ITJ18", "GRPJ12"),
            ("TPMH13", "LRW7"), ("JUM9B", "EPWQ12B"), ("TPMH13", "JTJT5B"),
            ("CMUA7", "TPMH13"), ("JXR1P", "TPMH13"), ("JUM9B", "LRW7"),
            ("VWC7B", "SGR15P"), ("EPWQ12B", "LRW7")
        ] if a in feats.ids and b in feats.ids
    ]
    
    # Remove one from each highly correlated pair
    for a, b in corr_pairs:
        if a in keep_ids and b in keep_ids:
            # Prefer the one with higher t-statistic
            ta = abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[:, feats.column(a)][feats.y==1], 
                                   feats.x[:, feats.column(a)][feats.y==0]).statistic)
            tb = abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[:, feats.column(b)][feats.y==1], 
                                   feats.x[:, feats.column(b)][feats.y==0]).statistic)
            if ta < tb:
                keep_ids.remove(a)
            else:
                keep_ids.remove(b)
    
    # Select top features by t-test
    selected = []
    for fid in feats.ids:
        if fid not in keep_ids:
            continue
        tstat = stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)][feats.y==1], 
                              feats.x[:, feats.column(fid)][feats.y==0]).statistic
        selected.append((fid, abs(tstat)))
    
    selected.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
    
    # Choose drivers (causes) - up to MAX_DRIVERS
    drivers = tuple(fid for fid, _ in selected[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # All features that might be useful for regression (limit to top 5)
    columns = tuple(fid for fid, _ in selected[:5])
    
    # Look for product terms between top features
    products = []
    # Only include product terms between top features
    top_features = set(columns)
    for a, b in corr_pairs:
        if a in top_features and b in top_features:
            products.append((a, b))
    
    # Simple weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for i, (fid, _) in enumerate(selected[:3]):
        loadings[fid] = 1.0 / (i + 1)
        
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
